newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladehs PM Hasina says Japan may increase aid.
newsitem.headline: Bangladehs PM Hasina says Japan may increase aid.

text.p: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Monday Japan had endorsed Bangladesh's economic policies and could raise its aid levels and boost investment in coming years.

"We have received a positive response from the Japanese government for increased aid and from private enterpreneurs for higher investment in Bangladesh," Hasina told a news conference after a six-day visit to Japan. She returned home on Sunday.
Hasina believed the visit had boosted the confidence of the Japanese about Bangladesh's economic potential and prospects for investment.
"We have signed an agreement on protection and promotion of investment during my visit to reassure the Japanese about Bangladesh's sincerity to work for mutual benefit," she said.
She said the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund of Japan would provide 15.25 billion yen (US$136 million) to finance three road, bridge and irrigation development projects.
Hasina said Japan would study Bangladesh's case for assistance for a $5 billion dollar dam on the Ganges and a $300 million bridge over the river Rupsha in southern Khulna.
Bangladesh wants the dam for irrigation after it signed a landmark treaty on sharing water from the Ganges with India last year.
Hasina said Japan had already raised its aid to Bangladesh to $313 million in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) from $170 million in the previous year.
"The Japanese aid has increased because we assumed power through a peaceful election," she said.

Hasina's Awami League party won elections held in June last year under supervision of a neutral caretaker government, defeating the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia.

She said her government had since attracted $1.2 billion in investment in the energy sector alone. The prime minister said she was hopeful of a favourable investment climate in the country, despite the actions of the main opposition BNP.
An eight-hour strike by the BNP on Thursday paralysed the country as Hasina was pursuing the Japanese aid.

Hasina said she had meetings with Japanese private entrepreneurs on the investment climate in Bangladesh. "They (Japanese investors) also want to create a separate special industrial zone for them in Bangladesh," she said.
South Korean investors have already aquired land in Bangladesh's southern Chittagong to create such a zone.
